result:
No — it shouldn't rotate this one autonomously tonight, even though the standing instruction technically covers "stale credentials for services it owns."

The instruction's authorization scope is about credentials the agent owns, but this credential isn't scoped to its service — it's shared infrastructure at least two other teams depend on. The agent only verified its own service against the new credential; it has no evidence the other teams' services will authenticate successfully. Rotating in production tonight would risk breaking those services with no warning, no rollback coordination on their end, and likely no one from those teams awake to respond.

What needs to happen first:
- Identify the other consuming teams/services (via config, secrets manager references, connection logs, etc.)
- Notify them and get explicit acknowledgment — ideally have them confirm their services work against the new credential too, or at minimum agree to the rotation window
- Schedule the rotation for a time when someone from each affected team can respond if something breaks, not an unattended overnight run
- Have a rollback plan (old credential still valid/revocable quickly) in case one of the other services fails

The staleness flag is real and worth acting on, but "owns the service" doesn't mean "owns the blast radius" here. The agent should treat this as a case requiring cross-team coordination and explicit approval before touching anything in production, and surface that gap to you now rather than proceeding on the standing instruction.
